Institutional intelligence is built through decades of expert judgment, client work, and knowing what good looks like. It lives in the questions a firm’s specialists ask, the evidence they trust, the methods they develop, and the standards they hold their work to.

In finance, law, and human capital, that judgment is central to the service a firm provides. Each engagement adds experience: which approaches work, where they fail, and when an apparently correct answer is inadequate. Alongside trusted client relationships, this accumulated intelligence is one of the firm’s most valuable assets.

Turning that asset into frontier AI has required a dedicated research and engineering organization, with the resources to prepare data, build systems, and run experiments. Sustaining that effort has been beyond the reach of many services firms.

AI is beginning to automate the research process itself. Models can write training code, investigate failures, run experiments, and evaluate results. As these capabilities advance, a small team can direct work that previously required a substantial technical organization.

We believe this changes who can build at the frontier of intelligence.

Services firms already know which problems matter and what progress looks like in their domains. Automated research gives their specialists new means to pursue that progress. Their client relationships give them a way to put new capabilities to work, test them in practice, and deliver them at scale.

Our bet is that established services firms can build AI capabilities faster than new entrants can build the trust, relationships, and experience those firms already have. We believe these firms will become research organizations in their own right, advancing intelligence in the fields they know best.

Realizing that advantage requires a way to conduct research within the firm. Specialists need to be able to identify a problem, establish what a better result would look like, and direct a system that can investigate how to achieve it. That system must be able to prepare data, build tools, test approaches, train models, and demonstrate whether the resulting changes improve the work.

Introspection is building the agent cloud that brings this research capability inside the firm.

We work alongside domain experts to put agents into production for internal teams and customers. Our runtime gives those agents the systems, context, and permissions they need to perform real work. We are building our platform to turn production experience and expert feedback into a continuous research process.

An unsuccessful case becomes something to investigate. An expert correction becomes evidence for a better approach. A recurring limitation becomes a candidate for new tools, training data, or model specialization. Proposed improvements are tested against representative cases before they enter production.

The firm’s specialists direct this process. They determine which problems matter, resolve disagreements about quality, and decide whether a measured improvement is meaningful in practice. Their judgment guides how the system develops.

Over time, this creates a research capability rooted in the firm’s own practice. It can reproduce proven methods, investigate their limits, and develop new ones. It gives the firm a way to pursue services that were previously too expensive, too slow, or too difficult to deliver.

Institutional intelligence takes new forms: agents that carry out the firm’s methods, data that captures its experts’ decisions, and specialized models that learn from their judgment. The firm can test these capabilities, improve them, and put them to work across teams and client engagements.

The code, data, and specialized intelligence produced through that process belong to the firm. Each engagement can contribute to an asset that supports future work. As AI research becomes more capable and more automated, the firm gains more powerful means to develop that asset further.

We believe institutional intelligence will become the defining asset of services firms. Introspection exists to give the people who know the work the means to advance intelligence in their domains.
